structured.approach:
This attempt fixes all three G1 refusals and rewrites feat.brd in full.

1. SM-5 no longer says 'the only change to an existing function'. It now names both additive changes exactly as feat.classification records them ('Two changes touch existing behaviour, and both are additive'): CR-4, the optional argument on build_explanation_request; and CR-1, feed ingestion accepting the optional paid_date, with the new reject reason 'paid_date' and the new field Invoice.paid_date. The section 4 intro now lists the same two changes and the four new functions, citing feat.classification. OS-6 reads 'Changes to existing behaviour beyond the two additive changes'.
2. The R-AP-12 row no longer says the outcome 'delivers' the roadmap item. It says feat.fitment gives R-AP-12 as the linked roadmap item, and that feat.fitment's agent judgement is that the entry matches it. BQ-5 was reworded to match.
3. The auditability row and the strategy row are now labelled 'agent judgement, recorded in feat.fitment', with the underlying source facts kept separate. My own uncited sentence 'Every rule in this BRD is explicit' was removed.

I then ran the verifier again and applied all 7 wording findings:
- The FIT-Y-ROADMAP caveat (FQ-5) was added.
- The REQ-03 approvals are now shown as the SIMULATED gate decisions recorded in COMMUNICATION.md.
- BQ-9 'must stay distinct' became feat.fitment's recommendation.
- The category is attributed to the REQ-02 classification.
- The question-set intro no longer says every question was answered.
- S-1 now reads 'each paid invoice'.
- 'Primary' user became 'the users named in the ticket'.
- The four repositories now cite the feat.intake Source table.

claims.text: The BRD follows the template sections problem, business outcome, users, scope, out of scope, business rules, success measures, approvals.
The business need is: AP managers want to see which overdue invoices belong to vendors that usually pay late, so they can chase them first.
feat.fitment recommends Yes, with reason code FIT-Y-ROADMAP (its own code, no approved list, FQ-5). It gives R-AP-12 as the linked roadmap item and judges that the entry matches it.
The REQ-03 gate decisions were 'PM: approve by sim.pm' and 'Leadership: approve by sim.leadership', and gates in this run are SIMULATED.
The REQ-04 BRD gate is Leadership, and the owner of this step is PM.

Current capability: ap_aging computes aging buckets (current, 1-30, 31-60, 61-90, 90+) for open invoices. Strategy: help finance teams pay on time and avoid late-payment penalties; auditability and traceability are core product promises.
The strategy fit and the auditability fit are agent judgement recorded in feat.fitment.

Two changes touch existing behaviour, and both are additive: build_explanation_request gains an optional argument (CR-4), and feed ingestion accepts the optional paid_date with a new reject reason and the new field Invoice.paid_date (CR-1). Four new functions are added.
The architecture rule is 'Keep every existing signature; add new functions'. The repositories named on the source item are ap_pipeline, ap_forecast, ap_aging and ap_portal.
Vendor risk is 'high' when predict_delay_days(history) > 30, 'medium' when > 10, otherwise 'low'. It uses no LLM.
The overdue list covers unpaid invoices more than 30 days past due, sorted by days descending then id. Vendors not in risk_by_vendor get 'unknown'.
The portal renders <table class="overdue-risk"> with one <tr class="risk-RISK"> per row, showing id, vendor, days and amount to two decimals, and an empty string when there are no rows.
Invoice amount is Decimal, 2 dp. JSON between services carries amounts as strings with two decimals. ap_portal is Node.js.
Monetary amounts use Decimal, never float, and Decimal arithmetic is kept.
No finance posting, authentication, tenancy or payment execution is in this change. Tier is T2, and the risk label is advisory only.
R-AP-14 (aging export) is out of scope. The regulatory 'Late' label (more than 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2) is a different term, and feat.fitment recommends keeping the labels distinct.
Assumptions B-A2 to B-A5 and B-A7 come from pre-backlog assumptions A-1 to A-5.
Boundary tests are required at exactly 30 days.
org.templates contains the templates but no separate business question set, although the brief describes it as holding one.

open_questions: OQ-B1 (PM / Leadership): Confirm the business meaning of 'vendors that usually pay late' and 'chase them first' in an AP context (carried from FQ-1).
OQ-B2: Keep 'overdue' (more than 30 days) and the regulatory 'Late' (more than 60 days, REG-LPR-2026-4.2) as distinct labels.
OQ-B3: The inputs define no business KPI. What business measure should define success?
OQ-B4: Confirm calendar days for days past due in overdue_with_risk (D-2026-031), with the 30-day boundary tested (L-007).
OQ-B5 (PM): Should one overdue definition be shared with ZD-48501 and ZD-48211?
OQ-B6: How should an unpaid row that has a paid_date be handled?
OQ-B7: org.templates holds no business question set. Should an approved set be added?
OQ-B8: Should renderOverdueRisk HTML-escape vendor names and ids?
OQ-B9: Should the risk level appear as visible text in the portal, or only as the row class?
OQ-B10: How should ap_portal (Node.js) format the two-decimal amount string without converting it to binary floating point (D-2026-044)?
structured.summary:
I rewrote feat.brd in full to fix the three refusals:
- SM-5 now names both additive changes, CR-4 and CR-1, as feat.classification records them.
- R-AP-12 is described as the linked roadmap item that feat.fitment judges the entry matches. The BRD no longer says the outcome 'delivers' it.
- The strategy and auditability links are labelled as agent judgement recorded in feat.fitment.

A second verifier pass found 7 more wording overstatements, and I fixed all of them. These include the simulated REQ-03 approvals and the FIT-Y-ROADMAP caveat. The BRD keeps the 8 template sections, BR-1 to BR-16, the business question set, assumptions B-A1 to B-A7, open questions OQ-B1 to OQ-B10, and a validation check. The check finds no conflict with the decision log; its only gap is the missing business KPI. Nothing blocks.
